newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fischler says GMO farm products must be separated.
newsitem.headline: Fischler says GMO farm products must be separated.

text.p: European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Friday it was necessary to segregate genetically modified organisms (GMOs) otherwise consumers could not be sure about the food they ate.
Fischler said EU labelling rules specifying that products "may contain" GMOs would mean that producers would label nearly all food in this way.
"This would be of zero information value for consumers," Fischler said after addressing the Centre for European Policy Studies. He added that consumers would no longer have any choice.
Fischler played down growing U.S. opposition to draft EU proposals to segregate GMOs throughout the food chain, and said some tolerance could be allowed.
Commission officials said segregation was the only way to have meaningful labelling. EU rules were not discriminatory as they applied equally to domestic and imported products.
On Thursday, USDA Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said in London it was doubtful whether GMO and non-GMO products could be segregated and Washington would oppose any such EU move.
"As long as these products are safe, we will not tolerate their segregation," he said at an International Grains Council Meeting.
